name: serbian_01
context: A tweet in Serbian, posted between April 2013 and February 2015 and collected through the Twitter Search API near the largest cities where the language is spoken. Native speakers labelled each tweet by the emotional attitude of the person who posted it.

versions.analysis_for_next: Neutral is the largest gold class (240/600), but the model predicts it only 141 times. 87 neutral tweets went to positive and 75 to negative. The model over-reads emotion in jokes, witty observations, teasing, everyday chatter and replies with emoticons. These annotators call many of those neutral: one-liners, absurd observations, aphorisms, mild complaints about school or sleep, hypotheticals, rhetorical questions and banter with :) or :D. Positive needs real joy, love, excitement or praise. Negative needs real distress, anger, insult or contempt. Swearing, caps or a smiley alone should not decide the label. A second pattern is in news headlines and links. Annotators often label them by the valence of the reported event: murders, arrests and scandals are negative, while awards, wins, new releases and promotions are positive. Purely procedural or schedule items stay neutral. A third pattern is self-deprecation: tweets where the poster calls themselves ugly, stupid or a failure, or says they are frustrated, tend to be negative even when written as a joke. Mocking compliments such as 'lepo je sto ih kristina savetuje' are negative. I will rewrite the question to make neutral the default for low-intensity or ambiguous humour. I will require clear intensity for positive and negative, add the headline-valence rule, and update examples and cues.

Version 1 overcorrected. Predicted neutral rose from 141 to 344, while gold neutral is 240. Negative recall fell from 145 to 115, with 100 negative tweets now labelled neutral. Positive recall fell from 79 to 56, with 64 positive tweets labelled neutral. Neutral precision is now poor. The missed negatives are mostly mild, wry grumbles and sarcasm: 'Mrzim ponedeljak' (I hate Monday), waking-up and studying woes, internet trouble, being bored, mocking couples or Facebook habits, and ironic political or media remarks. They also include self-deprecating anecdotes about failures and sarcastic 'Volim kad...' (I love it when...) complaints. These annotators treat any complaint, gripe, mockery or self-put-down as negative, even when it is phrased as a joke. The missed positives are warm, low-key tweets: greetings and shout-outs with ;) or :), loud laughter (HAHAHA), cheering ('Ajmoo'), wishes and daydreams, compliments to friends ('do jaja si' / you're awesome), enjoying drinking or partying, and upbeat headlines or promos. Neutral should be kept for texts with no evaluative lean: plain information, plans, questions, quotes or aphorisms without warmth or complaint, and jokes that neither gripe nor show warmth. The rule should be: decide the lean first, and use neutral only when there is none.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 2 swung too far toward negative. It predicted 360 negatives against 222 gold, and neutral recall collapsed to 71/240. Version 1 had the opposite problem, with too many neutral predictions. Neutral tweets misread as negative are mainly of four kinds. Some are witty generalisations about people, the sexes, age or social media. Some are absurd or hyperbolic stories about oneself. The rest are teasing banter and opinions without open contempt. Version 3 sits in the middle. Negative requires the poster's own clear displeasure or a sharp sarcastic jab. Positive requires clear warmth. Headlines follow the reported event. I trimmed the earlier draft to stay under 400 words.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 3 (56.6) nearly matched version 1 (56.9) but still overpredicts neutral: 311 neutral predictions against 240 gold. Negative recall is only 123/222. 93 negatives went to neutral. Most of them are ironic or sarcastic jokes. Some are self-mocking anecdotes ('Moje pauze od ucenja traju duze nego samo ucenje' / my study breaks last longer than the studying, 'Ponašam se kao tinejdžerka...' / I act like a teenager...). Others mock people's habits (couples' shared Facebook profiles, guys posing by cars, 'Dve stvari koje zene najvise zele' / two things women want most) or make dry political or media irony. Version 3 told the model that witty generalisations and absurd self-anecdotes are neutral, and that hurt negative recall. The reverse case, neutral tweets labelled negative, is mostly earnest rants and opinions, and these annotators label much of that neutral, so the data is noisy. Positive recall is low (61/138). Missed positives are upbeat shares and promotions: new songs, collections, magazine issues, sports news, applause. Others are wishes and daydreams, playful laughter, and affectionate greetings. Version 4 makes irony, sarcasm, self-mockery and mocking jokes about people's habits negative, even when they are light. Neutral stays for plain information, plans, questions, neutral banter, aphorisms and earnest statements of opinion. Positive also covers upbeat promotions, wishes and laughter. The wording is moderate so it does not repeat version 2's swing.

versions.analysis_for_next: Versions 1, 3 and 4 all score about 56.5 to 57. The development labels are noisy, so the remaining gain lies in balancing the two big confusions between neutral and negative. Version 3 predicted negative 196 times and missed 93 negatives. Version 4 predicted negative 341 times, sending 121 neutrals there, though it gained positive recall (67). Version 4's neutral-to-negative errors are mostly of two kinds: puns and wordplay ('Igraš košarku za Zadar, prezivaš se Šutalo...' / you play for Zadar, your name is Šutalo..., 'Koliko seljaka poznajem...' / I know so many peasants..., 'Medjunarodna skracenica za...Kinu je PRC' / the international abbreviation for China is PRC). The others are absurd, exaggerated self-anecdotes without a real failing (rolling into Tajikistan, pickles at 4 am, frozen fingers, the eye twitch at the cashier). These annotators call those neutral. The negatives version 4 gained, and should keep, are self-mockery that admits a real failing (laziness, procrastination, stupidity, ugliness), mocking people's habits and looks, sarcastic praise, and political or media irony. Version 5 keeps version 4's irony-is-negative stance but narrows it. Wordplay, puns and absurd exaggeration are neutral. A tie-break goes to neutral when there is no clear target of ridicule, no admitted failing and no displeasure word. Version 4's positive guidance on upbeat shares, wishes and laughter stays.

versions.analysis_for_next: Versions 1 and 3 to 5 all score about 56 to 57. The trade-off between neutral and negative has reached its noise ceiling. Version 3 put more borderline tweets in neutral, while versions 4 and 5 sent 110 to 121 neutral tweets to negative. Positive is the weakest class: recall is 56 to 71 out of 138 in every version, and most misses go to neutral. Three kinds of positive tweets keep being missed. (1) Shares and headlines about entertainment, sport, culture, fashion or products: a contract extension, player of the year, a fashion collection, LEGO film scenes, a new magazine issue, a novel promotion, a new song. (2) Aphorisms with a positive theme of beauty, happiness, love or friendship ('Lepota je ulaznica...' / beauty is a ticket..., 'Samo je malo potrebno da bi bio srecan' / it takes little to be happy, 'Neke prijatelje...volim vise nego...rodbine' / I love some friends more than relatives). (3) Wishes and daydreams. Gold labels for aphorisms seem to follow the valence of their theme: sad sayings were negative ('Najveća tuga je...' / the greatest sadness is...). Version 6 goes back to version 3's moderate split between neutral and negative, so jokes, wordplay, absurd anecdotes and earnest opinions are neutral. It keeps sarcasm, mock praise, ridicule of habits, admitted failings and explicit displeasure as negative. It also adds two positive rules. Upbeat or lifestyle shares about sport, entertainment, culture or products are positive. Sayings take the valence of their theme. Political or procedural announcements stay neutral and crime stays negative.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 6 hurt neutral badly: recall fell to 73. The rule that upbeat lifestyle or entertainment headlines are positive produced many false positives. Gold-neutral examples include the student film festival, a business tip, the documentary announcement, the SBB giveaway, a notice for coaches, a tennis score and 'Harden menja Brajanta' (Harden replaces Bryant). The rule that sayings take their theme's valence also misfired. 'Pogledaj u ogledalo...' (look in the mirror...), 'Dobro možeš da podeliš...' (you can share the good...) and 'Najveće istine čuješ od ludaka' (you hear the greatest truths from madmen) are gold neutral. Positive recall rose to 81, but this did not make up for the loss. The best versions are 1 (56.9) and 3 (56.6). Both make neutral the default for low-intensity content and require clear feeling for the other two labels. Version 7 goes back to that design. Neutral is the default for jokes, observations, absurd anecdotes, banter, aphorisms, opinions and routine announcements, including cultural and sports news. Positive requires clear warmth, joy, praise, cheering or explicitly good news such as a win or award. Negative requires clear personal displeasure, sadness, self-put-down (ugly, stupid, failure) or a pointed sarcastic or mocking jab at someone, and crime or scandal headlines are negative.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 7 tightened the neutral default and dropped to 55.1. Positive recall fell to 52 and negative recall stayed at about 120. Every version so far lands between 53 and 57. The swings between neutral and negative (versions 3, 4 and 5) trade errors almost one for one, so most of what remains there is annotator noise. Positive is the most improvable class, but the broad headline rule in version 6 created many false positives. The positives that are still missed, and are safe to fix, use explicitly positive wording rather than just a positive topic: 'sa zadovoljstvom...uživati' (with pleasure... enjoy), 'biće mnogo dobrih filmova' (there will be many good films), 'Top institucije kulture' (top cultural institutions), 'živeo današnji dan!' (long live today!), 'Imam neke pesme koje mi...poprave raspoloženje' (some songs instantly lift my mood). Also missed are pleasant wishes and daydreams ('Da stavim trajnu sminku, da se budim prelepa' / permanent make-up to wake up beautiful) and warm greetings ('Pozdrav za...;)' / greetings to... ;)). Version 8 starts from version 3, the best balanced split between neutral and negative. It adds three negative cases that version 4 caught: mocking jokes about people's habits, sarcastic praise, and self-mockery admitting a failing. It keeps puns and absurd anecdotes neutral. For positive, it uses explicit positive wording, pleasant wishes and warm greetings as the trigger, not the topic, so neutral announcements stay neutral.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 8 scored 55.5. Since version 1, every version has fallen between 53 and 57, and changes between neutral and negative trade errors almost one for one, which points to annotator noise. Version 1 scored highest (56.9), using a firm neutral default for low-intensity content and requiring clear intensity for positive and negative. Version 3, a close variant, scored 56.6. Broader rules for negative irony (versions 2, 4, 5, 8) or for positive topics (version 6) each moved a large block of neutral tweets into the wrong class. For the last version I return almost exactly to version 1, which had the best balance. I add only two small, low-risk refinements that version 1 did not cover explicitly. Positive includes promotions worded with explicit enthusiasm such as 'uživati' (enjoy) or 'sjajno' (great), but not plain announcements. Negative includes sarcastic praise and calling oneself stupid or a failure. Everything else stays as in version 1.

Version 9 (56.6) nearly matches version 1 (56.9) on the boundary between neutral and negative, but positive recall is only 50/138, giving positive F1 of about 0.47. The positive misses are mostly low-key warmth that the strict neutral default absorbs. Examples are greetings and shout-outs ('Pozdrav za...;)' / greetings to... ;)), thanks and replies to well-wishes ('hvala bratu na lepim zeljama' / thanks bro for the kind wishes), friendly compliments ('do jaja si' / you're awesome), and loud laughter (HAHAHA, 'pomrli od smeha' / we died laughing). Others are cheering ('Ajmoo'), warm wishes to followers (':*'), 'živeo' (long live), daydreams, enjoying drinks or going out, and uplifting sayings about happiness or beauty. Version 2, which counted such warmth as positive, reached positive F1 of about 0.53 despite lower precision. Positive is the class that can still gain without disturbing the other two. The final version keeps version 9's boundary between neutral and negative unchanged. It makes positive cover warmth even when low-key: greetings, thanks, compliments, laughter, cheering, warm wishes and daydreams. It keeps the warnings that mock praise is negative and that plain announcements stay neutral.
